name: Teen Patti
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Standard rules. Players choose to play blind or seen
Bet in turn. When only two players remain, either can call a show
winner: Best standard hand. Trail > Pure sequence > Sequence > Colour > Pair > High card
notes: The baseline. Good default when nobody wants a twist.

name: AK47
joker: Every Ace, King, 4 and 7 is a joker
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Plays exactly like normal Teen Patti
Any A, K, 4 or 7 in your hand counts as whatever card helps you most
notes: 16 jokers in the deck. Trails and pure sequences are common, hand values run high.

name: Muflis
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Normal play, but the entire ranking is flipped
High card beats pair, pair beats sequence, and a trail is the worst hand possible
Within the same category, lower cards win (2-3-5 beats 4-6-9)
Ace counts as the highest card, so it hurts you
notes: Messes with instincts hard. Agree upfront whether A-2-3 counts as a sequence.

name: Best of Four
setup: Deal 4 cards face down to each player
Everyone looks at their 4 cards and discards 1 face down
play: The remaining 3 cards are your hand
Normal Teen Patti play from there
notes: Blind play is awkward here since you must look to discard. Usually everyone plays seen.

name: Chhota Joker
joker: Each player's own lowest card is their personal joker
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Look at your hand and find your lowest ranked card
That card, and any other card of the same rank in your hand, becomes a joker for you only
Every player has a different joker
notes: If your lowest card is part of a pair, both become jokers, which usually means a trail.

setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Card values: Ace = 1, numbered cards = face value, J/Q/K = 0
Your 3 cards form a 3 digit number and you can arrange them in any order
Aim to get as close to 999 as possible
winner: The player whose number is closest to 999 wins
notes: Some groups play 'closest to 999 or 111' so a terrible hand can also win. Decide before dealing.

name: Joker Hunt
joker: Whatever rank the face-up card is
setup: Deal 3 cards to each player
Flip one card from the deck face up in the middle
play: All four cards of that rank become jokers for everyone
Normal play from there
notes: The shared joker means everyone is on the same footing, unlike Chhota Joker.

name: Sarphanchi
setup: Deal 1 card to each player
Without looking at it, hold it face out against your forehead
play: You can see everyone else's card but not your own
Bet based on what you see around the table
winner: Highest single card wins. Ace high
notes: Chaotic and loud, which is the point. Ends in seconds.

name: Jodi Bijodi
setup: Before dealing, the dealer declares 'odd' or 'even' for the round
Deal 3 cards to each player
play: If odd is declared, only odd cards (A, 3, 5, 7, 9, J, K) count toward your hand
If even, only even cards (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, Q) count
winner: Best hand made from your qualifying cards. Zero qualifying cards means you are out for the round
notes: Agree upfront where Ace sits. Most groups call it odd.

name: Do Raja
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Normal Teen Patti play, but there are two winners at the end
winner: The best hand and the worst hand both win. Muflis ranking decides the worst
notes: Keeps people in longer since a garbage hand is still live. Works well with a large table.

name: Gol Chakkar
setup: Deal 4 cards to each player
play: Everyone looks at their 4 cards and picks 1 from their own hand
Pass it face down to the player on your left. All passes happen at the same time, so you pass before seeing what comes to you
You now hold 5 cards. Discard 1 face down to make your final 3 card hand
Nobody touches the deck after the deal
notes: Dealer calls the pass direction (left or right) before the pass happens.

name: Char Sau Bees
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Card values: Ace = 1, numbers at face value, J/Q/K = 0
Arrange your 3 cards in any order to form a 3 digit number
winner: Closest to 420 wins, over or under
notes: Sister game to 999 but less obvious, since going past 420 is possible. More thinking, more arguing.

name: Padosi
joker: The flipped rank plus the rank directly above and below it
setup: Deal 3 cards to each player
Flip one card face up
play: If a 7 is flipped, all 6s, 7s and 8s are jokers. 12 jokers total
Ace wraps around, so an Ace flip makes K, A and 2 wild
notes: The near-misses are the fun part. People realise their card was one rank off.

name: Tukka
joker: Each player's own called rank, personal to them
setup: Before any cards are dealt, every player calls out a rank out loud so it is locked
Deal 3 cards to each player
play: Your called rank is your personal joker for the round
Everyone has a different one and everyone knows everyone else's
notes: You commit blind, so it is genuinely 50-50 whether it helps. Table reads get loud.

name: Jodi Joker
joker: Conditional, based on your own hand shape
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: If your hand contains a natural pair, your third card automatically becomes a joker
If you have no pair, you get no joker at all
notes: Every pair silently upgrades to a trail. Half the table thinks they are unbeatable, then four trails hit the show at once.

name: Badalta Joker
setup: Deal 3 cards to each player
Flip one card face up. That rank is wild
play: After each betting round, flip a new card
The new rank replaces the old one entirely. The previous joker goes dead
Cap it at three flips total
winner: Best standard hand using whatever the final joker is
notes: Your hand goes from garbage to trail to garbage across three flips. Keep the cap or the round drags.

name: Laal Kaali
joker: Every card of the flipped card's colour
setup: Deal 3 cards to each player
Flip one card face up
play: If the flip is red, all 26 red cards are jokers
If black, all 26 black cards. Half the deck goes wild
notes: Almost everyone lands a trail. Peak chaos. The natural-beats-joker tiebreak matters most here.

name: Beat the B*tch
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to the middle as the side hand. Nobody looks at it
Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Play a full classic Teen Patti round among the players
Once one player has won the round, reveal the side hand
The round winner must beat the side hand with their own hand
winner: The round winner takes the pot only if their hand beats the side hand. If the side hand wins or ties, nobody takes the pot and it rolls over into the next round
notes: Pot can roll over several rounds and get big. Decide upfront whether a tie counts as a loss (recommended: yes).

name: Sabka Hissa
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
Flip 1 card face up in the middle before betting starts
play: The flipped card belongs to every player at the table
At showdown, each player plays their best 3 out of their own 3 cards plus the shared card
winner: Best standard hand using your best 3 of 4 cards
notes: The one variation where the dealer's flip helps the whole table instead of picking a winner or a victim.

name: Bhoot Wale Patte
setup: Dealer secretly sets aside 2 cards face down before dealing, unseen by anyone including the dealer
Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Play a fully normal round, betting and folding as usual, down to the final two players
At the show, reveal both secret cards. Those 2 ranks are cursed for this hand
Either finalist holding a cursed rank is disqualified instantly, regardless of hand strength
winner: The clean finalist wins automatically if the other is cursed. If both are clean, best standard hand wins. If both are cursed, the pot rolls into the next hand
notes: A trail of Aces can still lose if Aces turn out to be cursed. The best hand in the room can lose without a single comparison.

name: Kismat Ka Jugad
setup: Boot for this hand is double the usual amount
Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: First betting round plays as normal
To exchange 1 card from your hand for a fresh one from the deck, you must first double the current chaal
Discard the unwanted card face down and draw a replacement
Capped at 2 swaps total per player for the whole hand
Normal betting continues between swaps
notes: Paying double to sit in, then double again to fix your hand, is either smart play or a trap. Usually a trap.
